statement:
The simple acyclic envelopes used in R2 — For every infinite cardinal $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ and group $H$ with
$|H|\leq\lambda$, there is an embedding $H\hookrightarrow C$ with $C$
nonabelian simple, integrally acyclic, and $|C|=\lambda$.

The complete mapping-space assertion A4 — Let $t:X\to W$ be an acyclic map of connected CW complexes, let
$P=\ker\pi_1(t)$, and let $Y$ be any $\mathcal U$-small space, possibly
disconnected or empty. Restriction is a weak equivalence
\[
 t^*:\operatorname{Map}(W,Y)\ \longrightarrow\
 \operatorname{Map}(X,Y)_{P=1},
\]
where the right side is the union of those components represented by maps
$f:X\to Y$ whose induced fundamental-group homomorphism kills $P$.
In particular this holds for every resolution $BG\to W$ in R2.

Step-by-step confirmation of R2, Proof 2 — Let $W$ be a connected $\mathcal U$-small CW complex and
$\mu\in\mathcal U$ a cardinal. There is an acyclic map $t:BG\to W$
whose fundamental-group map is onto with perfect kernel $P$, and every
homomorphism $G\to L$ with $|L|\leq\mu$ kills $P$.
If $W$ has a simplicial model with $\nu$ simplices, the construction
uses at most $\max(\aleph_0,\mu^+,\nu)$ cells and a group of at most
that cardinality.

The size lemma and the repair of R2, Proof 1 — For every connected CW complex $E$ with at most an infinite cardinal
$\lambda$ of cells, there is an acyclic map $BH\to E$ with
$|H|\leq\lambda$ and a classifying model with at most $\lambda$ cells.
With this lemma, every step of \texttt{OWN\_RESULTS.md}, Theorem 3.1,
is valid. Its recalled bound is supplied here by the later metric
Kan--Thurston theorem, rather than attributed to the original
Kan--Thurston construction.

A relative form of the checked construction — Let $f:BH\to W$ be a based map of connected $\mathcal U$-small CW
complexes, with $BH$ aspherical and $f_*:H\to\pi_1W$ onto. There are
an embedding $j:H\hookrightarrow G$ and an acyclic map $t:BG\to W$
such that $tBj=f$ in a CW model containing $BH$ as a subcomplex.
For an infinite $\lambda$ bounding the cells of $BH$ and $W$, all
models and groups can be chosen of size at most $\lambda$.

A simple kernel can be imposed in R2 — Let $W$ be connected and $\mathcal U$-small, and let $\mu\in\mathcal U$.
For every infinite cardinal $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ with
$\lambda>\mu$ and with a $\lambda$-cell CW model of $W$, there is an
acyclic map $t:BG\to W$ with
\[
 |G|=|P|=\lambda,\qquad
 P=\ker(\pi_1t:G\twoheadrightarrow\pi_1W)
\]
and $P$ nonabelian simple. Consequently every homomorphism from $G$
to a group of cardinality at most $\mu$ kills $P$.

The kernel's homology is determined by the target — For every acyclic map $t:BG\to W$ with $W$ connected and
$P=\ker\pi_1t$, pulling back the universal cover of $W$ gives a
$\pi_1W$-equivariant acyclic map
\[
 BP\longrightarrow\widetilde W.
\]
It induces $\mathbb Z[\pi_1W]$-module isomorphisms
$H_n(P;\mathbb Z)\cong H_n(\widetilde W;\mathbb Z)$ for every $n$.
The action on the left is conjugation through $G/P$.
For fixed $W$, these are exactly the possible graded homology modules
of kernels in R2, including R2 with a nonabelian simple kernel.

Functoriality for injective maps and for all simplicial maps — Fix an infinite $\lambda\in\mathcal U$. The construction in A.3 can be
chosen as a functor on ordered simplicial complexes and simplicial maps
that are injective and order-preserving on every simplex. Its maps to
geometric realization are natural. Precomposing with barycentric
subdivision gives this assertion for arbitrary simplicial complexes
and all maps injective on every simplex, in particular for injective
simplicial maps.

There is also a functor $\widehat T_\lambda$ on all
$\mathcal U$-small simplicial complexes and all simplicial maps, with a
natural acyclic map $\widehat T_\lambda(K)\to |K|$, aspherical
components, and the no-small-quotient conclusion for groups of
cardinality $<\lambda$. It has at most
$\max(\lambda,\aleph_0,|K|)$ cells. This last functor uses the explicit
resolution below; it does not identify the original simplex cones
with their replacements.

The limits of simultaneous functorial strengthening — The original simple-cone construction, with
$T(\Delta^n)\simeq BC_n$ and subcomplex group injections, cannot extend
to a functor on all ordered simplicial maps while keeping those
values and maps. Moreover, no acyclic-resolution functor on all
connected spaces and maps can have a nonabelian simple kernel on
every simply connected space.

Dimension preservation for all finite target groups — Let $W$ be a connected CW complex of finite dimension $n$. There is
an acyclic map $t:BG\to W$ with a classifying model of dimension at
most $n$, such that every homomorphism $G\to F$ to a finite group
kills $\ker\pi_1t$. Thus the same resolution satisfies R2 for every
finite cardinal $\mu$. A finite, respectively countable, $W$ admits
a finite, respectively countable, resolving model. More generally,
an infinite bound on the cells of $W$ also bounds the cells of this
model and the cardinality of $G$.

The exact cardinal restriction for countable models — For any resolution $t:BG\to W$ with nontrivial kernel $P$, the
no-small-quotient assertion of R2 at $\mu$ implies $\mu<|G|$.
For countable finite-dimensional nonaspherical $W$, a countable
resolving model of dimension at most $\dim W$ satisfies R2 at
$\mu$ precisely for finite $\mu$, in the sense of existence of
such a model. Dimension alone imposes no bound on $\mu$ valid for
all $W$: the identity map of any connected graph satisfies R2 for
every $\mu$ and has the same dimension as its target.

Descent and the two proofs of R3 — The specified comparison in both supplied proofs of R3 is valid. The first proof also applies to any $\U$-small colimit of representables. In the second proof, filteredness is used precisely to preserve the injections induced by an acyclic map.

All invariant small colimits of representables — The $\Winfty$-invariant presheaves on $\Cathot_\U$ that are $\U$-small colimits of representables are exactly the presheaves
\[
 X\longmapsto\colim_{i\in I}\pi_0\Fun(\Pi_1X,G_i),
\]
where $I$ is any $\U$-small category and $G:I\to\Ho(\Grpd_\U)$ is a diagram. For an invariant presentation $H=\colim_i h_{K_i}$ the canonical comparison
\[
 \colim_i h_{K_i}\longrightarrow\colim_i h_{\Pi_1K_i} \tag{B.2.1}
\]
is an isomorphism of presheaves, for the original index $I$.

Truncation localizers — For every integer $n\geq1$, the $\W_n$-invariant $\U$-small ind-objects are exactly the ind-groupoids. The $\W_0$-invariant ones are exactly the ind-objects of discrete sets. Their canonical representatives are respectively $(\Pi_1K_i)_i$ and $(\pi_0K_i)_i$. For representable presheaves the corresponding classes consist of objects isomorphic in $\Cathot$ to groupoids and to discrete categories.

Integral homology and homologically local groups — Let $\mathcal G_{\mathbb Z}$ be the full subcategory of groupoids whose isotropy groups are local for the homomorphisms inducing an isomorphism on $H_1(-;\mathbb Z)$ and a surjection on $H_2(-;\mathbb Z)$. The $\W_{\mathbb Z}$-invariant $\U$-small ind-objects of $\Cathot$ are exactly the ind-objects of $\mathcal G_{\mathbb Z}$. Their canonical presentation is $(E_{\mathbb Z}\Pi_1K_i)_i$, where $E_{\mathbb Z}$ is groupwise integral homological localization. The invariant representables are exactly the categories isomorphic in $\Cathot$ to objects of $\mathcal G_{\mathbb Z}$.

The enlarged-universe classification — Restriction along $q:\Cathot_\U\to\Hot_\U$ gives an equivalence from $\Ind_\V(\Hot_\U)$ onto the full subcategory of $\Winfty$-invariant objects in $\Ind_\V(\Cathot_\U)$. In particular every $\U$-small homotopy type has a $\V$-small filtered ind-presentation on $\Cathot_\U$.

An exact algebraic classification for every larger localizer — Let $\W\supseteq\Winfty$ be any fundamental localizer in $\Cat_\U$. Let $\mathcal G=\Ho(\Grpd_\U)$ and let $S_{\W}$ be the class of arrows $\Pi_1u$ for $u\in\W$. Form the ordinary localization $q_{\W}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal D_{\W}=\mathcal G[S_{\W}^{-1}]$ in $\V$. Under the fully faithful embedding of ind-groupoids as presheaves, the exact class of invariant small ind-objects is
\[
 \Ind_\U(\mathcal G)\ \cap\
 q_{\W}^*\operatorname{PSh}(\mathcal D_{\W}). \tag{B.6.1}
\]
Here the intersection is an intersection of essential images inside presheaves on $\mathcal G$. Its membership is given by the explicit extension and equality tests below. For representables, it consists of groupoids $G$ satisfying the displayed algebraic bijection (B.6.2). These descriptions require no accessibility or reflectivity assumption on $\W$.

The sharp cardinal threshold for bounded tests — Let $\mu,\kappa\in\U$ be infinite cardinals, and let $K:I\to\Cathot_\U$ have $\U$-small filtered index and $|\Mor K_i|\leq\mu$ for every $i$. Among such presentations, invariance on all categories with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows forces the canonical global ind-groupoid isomorphism for every $K$ exactly in the range
\[
                         \mu^+<\kappa. \tag{B.7.1}
\]
Outside this range, every small homotopy type occurs on those tests using stages with at most $\mu$ arrows. In particular $K(C_2,2)$ gives a presentation that is invariant on the prescribed tests and has no global ind-groupoid isomorphism.

All bounded invariant restrictions — Fix an infinite $\kappa\in\U$, and let $\mathcal C_{<\kappa}$ be a skeleton of categories with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows, with transformation-homotopy morphisms. Its localization is denoted $\mathcal D_{<\kappa}$. The restrictions of small ind-objects that are invariant on these tests are exactly the presheaves on $\mathcal D_{<\kappa}$ whose pullbacks $F$ satisfy the following finite conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $F(\varnothing)$ is a singleton and $F(A\amalg B)\to F(A)\times F(B)$ is bijective;
\item for every pair $u,v:A\rightrightarrows B$, with $C$ the specified Grothendieck homotopy coequalizer of B.5 and $w:B\to C$, the function
\[
 F(C)\longrightarrow\Eq\bigl(F(B)\rightrightarrows F(A)\bigr)
\]
is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
Every such restriction has a presentation by stages with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows. For $\kappa>\aleph_0$, these classes are equivalently $\Ind_\U(\Hot_{<\kappa})$, where a type belongs to $\Hot_{<\kappa}$ when it has a simplicial model of size less than $\kappa$. For $\kappa=\aleph_0$, the two displayed finite conditions give the classification directly on the localization of finite categories.

The categories and their comparison maps — Let $\tau=\varepsilon_1\cdots\varepsilon_n$ be a finite sign word,
including the empty word. Its interval $I_\tau$ is the free category
on the oriented line with vertices $0,\ldots,n$. A type map is an
endpoint-preserving functor with nondecreasing vertex function.
Write $\mathrm{Ty}$ for their category. Put
\[
 F_\tau(a,b)=\operatorname{Fun}_\Sigma(I_\tau,M)_{a,b},
 \qquad F_\tau^{\Sigma}(a,b)\subset F_\tau(a,b).
\]
Objects send backward edges into $\Sigma$. In $F_\tau$ the vertical
components are arbitrary, with both endpoint components identities;
in $F_\tau^\Sigma$ they all belong to $\Sigma$.
The fibred Grothendieck constructions are denoted by
$\operatorname{Ch}_\Sigma(M;a,b)$ and
$\operatorname{Ch}_\Sigma^\Sigma(M;a,b)$. A morphism $(\tau,c)\to
(\sigma,d)$ is a pair $(u,\eta)$ with
$u:\tau\to\sigma$ and $\eta:c\Rightarrow d u$.
The inclusion $J$ preserves literal concatenation and empty paths.

Step-by-step verification of PATHS C.P1 — For $\tau,\sigma\in\mathrm{Ty}$ the poset
$P(\tau,\sigma)$ of type maps, ordered by pointwise arrows in
$I_\sigma$, is empty or has contractible nerve. These posets form the
hom-categories of a strict monoidal $2$-category. There is a strict
contravariant action
\[
 P(\tau,\sigma)\times F_\sigma(a,b)\longrightarrow F_\tau(a,b).
\]

Descent, finality, and PATHS C.P2--C.P3 — Let $R$ be the reachability preorder of types. The diagram
$\tau\mapsto BF_\tau(a,b)$ descends coherently along
$p:\mathrm{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}}\to R^{\mathrm{op}}$.
The functor $p$ is homotopy final. Every projective sequence
$t:\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ty}$ such that each type
receives a map from some $t_n$ is homotopy final after passage to
$R$. For its actual Grothendieck construction $E_t$ and categorical
colimit $C_\infty(t)$ both maps
\[
 C_\infty(t)\longleftarrow E_t\longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Ch}_\Sigma(M;a,b)
\]
are weak equivalences. The resulting isomorphism $\beta_t$ in
$\mathrm{Hot}$ is canonical, natural under strictly commuting maps
of sequences, and transitive under the comparisons through $t*s$.

The actual padding and gluing operations — For a block $\tau_0$ containing both signs, the left, right and
symmetric systems of VII ms.~125--126 have weakly equivalent
colimits $L,R,P$. The actual constant-padding maps $q_L:L\to P$
and $q_R:R\to P$ are weak equivalences. On each endpoint fibre,
\[
 \mu=B\kappa\bigl((Bq_L)^{-1}\times(Bq_R)^{-1}\bigr)
\]
is associative, unital, and independent of the block under the
specified comparisons in $\mathrm{Hot}$.

Exact one-sign answer at VII ms.~125--127 — For every integer $d\geq1$, the left, right and symmetric colimits
formed with the block $+^d$ are isomorphic in $\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathrm{hot}}$
to $\operatorname{Hom}_M(a,b)_{\mathrm{disc}}$; those formed with
$-^d$ are isomorphic there to
$\operatorname{Hom}_\Sigma(b,a)_{\mathrm{disc}}$.
Both actual padding maps are isomorphisms in
$\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathrm{hot}}$. The operation induced by gluing is
associative, unital, and independent of $d$ within either sign.
It is ordinary composition in $M$ in the positive case and
composition in $\Sigma^{\mathrm{op}}$ in the negative case.

The comparison with the all-type localization mapping space, at
every pair of endpoints, is an equivalence for positive blocks
exactly when $\Sigma\subset\operatorname{Iso}(M)$, and for
negative blocks exactly when $M=\Sigma$ is a groupoid.

The crown and the scope of the one-sign failure — For the four-object poset with nonidentity arrows
$0\to1,0\to3,2\to1,2\to3$, mark all arrows and take $a=b=0$.
Every nonempty one-sign fixed-type path category is a point, whereas
the all-type mapping space has component set $\mathbb Z$.
Thus one-sign blocks do not in general compute the all-type object
or provide the comparison with a mixed block. They nevertheless
have the padding and associative unital composition proved in C.5.

R7 F2, with both adjunctions checked — For every small $(M,\Sigma)$ as above and $a,b\in M$, there is an
equivalence
\[
 B\operatorname{Ch}_\Sigma(M;a,b)\simeq
 \operatorname{Map}_{L(M,\Sigma)}(a,b).
\]
For fixed $b$ it is an equivalence of presheaves under
$h_b=\operatorname{Hom}_M(-,b)$, after the explicit presheaf
replacement below. Each single-type map $h_b\to X_b^\tau$
is already an equivalence after localization of presheaves at
$\Sigma$.

The specified map $Q$, both endpoint variables, and composition — The canonical map $Q_{a,b}$ of PATHS B.6 is the equivalence in C.7.
These maps are natural in $a\in M^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $b\in M$,
with coherent endpoint actions, and preserve composition, units,
and all their coherences. They identify the operation of C.4 with
composition in $L(M,\Sigma)$.

F3 and the restricted-vertical inclusion — For every wide $\Sigma$, the specified inclusion
$J:\operatorname{Ch}_\Sigma^\Sigma(M;a,b)\to
\operatorname{Ch}_\Sigma(M;a,b)$ is a weak equivalence.
The identification with Dwyer--Kan hammock localization is natural
in both endpoints, under the ordinary arrows and the empty paths,
and compatible with concatenation.

Finite verification of the stated formulas — The attached independent program verifies the two descriptions of
type maps on all $961$ pairs of words of length at most four, their
contravariant composition on $2731$ composable pairs of maps with
word lengths at most three, the run-clamping formulas on $1213$
nonempty mapping posets, the one-sign crown calculation for $224$
marking/length/sign choices, and $16$ strictly commuting padding
squares for the block $(+,-,+)$. It also verifies the integral
certificate used in C.11 on $7937$ arrows to $1023$ target words.

R8 with an explicit integral obstruction — The category $\mathrm{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is isomorphic to the
category of finite sign words with nondecreasing sign-preserving
letter maps. For $p=(++)$, $q=(+-+)$, the two arrows
$e=(1,3),c=(1,1):p\rightrightarrows q$ have no completion to a
commutative square. They have no affine equalizer over any nonzero
unital ring. The covariant set-valued quotient
\[
 H=\mathrm{Ty}^{\mathrm{op}}(p,-)/(ge\sim gc)
\]
has $H_1(B\operatorname{El}(H);\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$.
In particular the opposite type category is not totally
$W_\infty$-aspherical, and categorical colimits over it do not
compute homotopy colimits for every diagram, even for diagrams of
sets.

Literature scope of the path comparison — The all-type equivalence of C.7--C.9 follows from the proofs above
and the specified hammock comparison, with no calculus-of-fractions
hypothesis. The primary sources opened for this section support the
comparisons summarized below. No priority is claimed.

The comparison on constants is the specified path comparison — For every cofinal path sequence $K_n=F_{t_n}(a,b)$, the path formula identifies $c_X$ with
\[
 \colim_n\pi_0\Fun(X,K_n)
 \longrightarrow[BX,Z_{a,b}],
\]
induced by evaluation and the maps $BK_n\to Z_{a,b}$ of C.8. This equality is natural in $X$, $a$, and $b$, and preserves composition.

Equivalent exact criteria for invariance — For the fixed pair $a,b$, the following conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $H_{a,b}$ inverts all nerve weak equivalences in $\Cat_\U$.
\item For every stage $n$, there are $m\geq n$ and a functor $r_n:\Pi_1K_n\to K_m$ such that
\[
 [r_n\eta_{K_n}]=[K_n\to K_m]\quad\text{in }\Cathot.
\]
\item $Z_{a,b}$ is a $1$-type, and for every $X$ the square of sets
\[
 \begin{array}{ccc}
 H_{a,b}(\Pi_1X)&\xrightarrow{c_{\Pi_1X}}&[B\Pi_1X,Z_{a,b}]\\
 \downarrow&&\downarrow\\
 H_{a,b}(X)&\xrightarrow{c_X}&[BX,Z_{a,b}]
 \end{array} \tag{C.14.1}
\]
is cartesian. The vertical maps are the specified restrictions along $\eta_X$.
\end{enumerate}
Applying these conditions to every pair of objects classifies the requested small relative categories. Condition (ii) is independent of the chosen cofinal sequence.

A finite relative example with a nontrivial mapping-space fundamental group — For any small groupoid $G$, form $M$ by adjoining objects $a,b$, with no arrows between them, no arrows from $G$ to them, and one arrow from each of $a,b$ to every object of $G$. Mark all morphisms in the full cone $\{b\}*G$ and the identity of $a$. Then, for every small $X$,
\[
 H_{a,b}(X)\cong\pi_0\Fun(X,G),\qquad
 \Map_{L(M,\Sigma)}(a,b)\simeq BG. \tag{C.15.1}
\]
The comparison sends a functor $g:X\to G$ to the roof $a_X\to g\leftarrow b_X$. In particular $G=\mathbf BC_2$ gives a finite relative category and a connected invariant mapping space with fundamental group $C_2$.

The scope of full comparison functors — Bijectivity of the constant-to-constant Hom comparisons $c_X$ for all $X$, together with $1$-truncated mapping spaces, is a sufficient instance of C.14. Full equivalence of the entire categories $\alpha_X$ is a stronger hypothesis than the one used by that criterion. The exact required condition is cartesianness of (C.14.1), not a statement about the other objects or Hom-sets of $\alpha_X$.

D.K5 with two complete proofs and its exact marking convention — Let $t:\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ty}$ be a sequence
such that every type receives a map from some $t_n$, and put
$K_n=F_{t_n}(a,b)$ with its actual pullback transitions. For every
small $M$, wide composition-closed $\Sigma$, and small $X$, effect
of a localization word induces a natural bijection
\[
 \operatorname{colim}_{n}\pi_0\operatorname{Fun}(X,K_n)
       \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H_{a,b}(X).                 \tag{C.20.1}
\]
It respects concatenation, the constant paths, and restriction in
$X$. Containing all identities and being closed under composition
are exactly the conditions on a class of arrows that make these
path categories stable under every type pullback.

Complete classification of projective sequences of types — For a projective sequence $t$, let $r_n$ be the number of maximal
constant-sign runs of $t_n$, with zero for the empty word. The
following three conditions are equivalent: the $r_n$ are unbounded;
every type receives a map from some $t_n$; and (C.20.1) is a
bijection for every small relative category, all endpoint pairs,
and every small $X$.

Every sequence outside this class is eventually, after passing to
$\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathrm{hot}}$ on its path fibres, constant at the
fibre of one finite alternating word $\sigma$. More precisely,
for every $(M,\Sigma),a,b,X$ there is a canonical bijection
\[
 \operatorname{colim}_n\pi_0\operatorname{Fun}(X,F_{t_n}(a,b))
      \cong\pi_0\operatorname{Fun}(X,F_\sigma(a,b)),        \tag{C.21.1}
\]
commuting with effect in the localization. Consequently, for any
fixed data outside the universal domain, (C.20.1) holds exactly
when every localization word from $a_X$ to $b_X$ has a
$\sigma$-representative and any two such representatives with
the same effect are connected by endpoint-fixed $\sigma$-ladders.
These are respectively the exact existence and equality conditions
for this finite type; no claim that they always hold is made.

The type formalism and its actual colimits — The corrected type category at VII ms.~26--32 has
endpoint-preserving, nondecreasing interval functors, and its path
construction is the fibred construction of C.1. Its concatenation
is strictly associative and unital. Its empty word is terminal.
The opposite type category is neither filtered nor totally
$W_\infty$-aspherical. In contrast every sequential path colimit
$C_\infty(t)$ is indexed covariantly by the filtered category
$\mathbb N$, regardless of cofinality of $t$.

For a sequence of full subcategory inclusions $K_n\subset K_{n+1}$,
every $X$ with finitely many objects satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{colim}_n\operatorname{Fun}(X,K_n)
       \cong\operatorname{Fun}(X,\operatorname{colim}_nK_n).
                                                               \tag{C.22.1}
\]
For arbitrary filtered diagrams the same assertion holds for
categories $X$ with finitely many arrows. These are statements
in $\mathrm{Cat}$ and on taking components; the map to derived
mapping classes is the further specified comparison $c_X$ of C2.

VII \S10: the uniform criterion and its path-specific replacement — For small $u:J\to T$, the projection of fibred total categories
\[
 p_F:\int_J^{\mathrm{fib}}Fu^{\mathrm{op}}
               \longrightarrow\int_T^{\mathrm{fib}}F
\]
is a weak equivalence for every strict $F:T^{\mathrm{op}}\to
\mathrm{Cat}$ exactly when $B(u/t)$ is weakly contractible for
every $t\in T$. The parallel-pullback homotopy, preorder filtration
and countability hypotheses of VII ms.~99--101 do not imply this
comparison. For path fibres over $\mathrm{Ty}$ the specified
comparison does hold, by C.2--C.3. The projection
$\mathrm{Ty}\to R$ is neither smooth nor proper, even for the
connected-component localizer, so neither sufficient criterion
proposed at VII ms.~112 supplies that path comparison.

V ms.~46--49: fibrant unions and ind-isomorphisms — Filtered colimits of Thomason-fibrant categories are
Thomason-fibrant, and objectwise weak equivalences of actual
filtered diagrams induce weak equivalences of colimits. There is,
however, a sequence of finite local Thomason-fibrant categories
with full inclusion transitions whose union $T$ is not local.
The union has an endofunctor $s$ inducing the identity ind-morphism
in $\operatorname{Ind}(\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathrm{hot}})$ but not a
weak equivalence. Thus the proposed implications at V ms.~47 and
the uniqueness claim at ms.~48--49 fail even with fibrant stages
and a fibrant union.

VII ms.~129--132: invariance is additional structure — Weak-equivalence invariance of $H_{a,b}$ can fail between finite
test categories for a finite relative category with every arrow
marked. Thus neither the existence of the mapping space in C.7
nor weak equivalence of a path category to a Thomason-fibrant
category implies this invariance. The canonical mapping-space
interpretation itself always holds, before making any invariance
assumption on $H_{a,b}$.
status: Refuted, with an explicit finite obstruction

statement:
IX ms.~22--23: the finite example and the loop test — The two-object category of pointed sets on the one- and two-element
pointed sets, marked only at identities, satisfies both
representabilities in test (a), global invariance in test (b), and
both pointed mapping-space formulas in test (c). Its localization
is not equivalent to a point. Thus the finite-category doubt at
ms.~23 is false under the hypotheses printed there.

Conversely there is a countable small relative category satisfying
both formulas in (c) for all objects while global invariance in
(b) fails. Thus the final assertion on ms.~23 that (b) is
necessary for (c) is also false. The exact positive statement is
that genuine homotopy pullbacks $\Omega b=0\times_b0$ and
homotopy pushouts $\Sigma a=0\amalg_a0$ in the localized
$\infty$-category give these formulas with all their loop
coherences, by the mapping-space universal properties.

Strict retraction in the prescribed weak-homotopy class — Let $A$ be Thomason-fibrant, let $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ be a Thomason cofibration, and let $p:B\to A$ satisfy $pi\simeq\mathrm{id}_A$ by a finite categorical homotopy. There is $r:B\to A$ with $ri=\mathrm{id}_A$ in $\mathrm{Cat}$ and $[r]=[p]$ in $\mathrm{Hot}$.

The local-target and groupoid cases — Under the hypotheses of D.1, a local target $A$ admits $r$ with $[r]=[p]$ in $\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathrm{hot}}$. For an actual groupoid target the same conclusion follows for every full inclusion $i$ that is injective on objects, without Thomason fibrancy or cofibration assumptions.

Prescribed fence extension for targets with a terminal object — Let $i:C\hookrightarrow D$ be a full sieve inclusion, let $F$ have a terminal object $t$, and let $f:D\to F$ and $H:C\times Z\to F$ agree on $C\times\{0\}$. There is an extension over $D\times Z'$ for a padding $Z'\to Z$ obtained by adding one edge at the initial position.

Prescribed fence extension for targets with an initial object — Let $i:C\hookrightarrow D$ be a pseudo-Dwyer inclusion. Choose its cosieve neighborhood $W\subseteq D$, a retraction $s:W\to C$, and a transformation $\varepsilon:is\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}_W$ whose restriction to $C$ is the identity. Let $F$ have an initial object $o$. Every pair $f:D\to F$, $H:C\times Z\to F$ agreeing at the initial endpoint admits the extension of D.3 after one padding edge. When $W=D$, the conclusion holds for every target $F$.

A non-cofibrant corner can still admit padded extension — Let $C=\{0\}$, $D=[1]$, and let $F$ be the three-object poset with arrows $o\to u$ and $o\to v$. The corner functor sending $(0,0)$ to $o$, $(1,0)$ to $u$, and $(0,1)$ to $v$ has no extension to $D\times[1]$. It extends over a padded fence with two edges. The category $F$ is Thomason-fibrant.

Fibrancy does not make the categorical comparison injective — There are a finite category $X$ with six objects and twenty-two arrows, a $\mathcal U$-small Thomason-fibrant poset $F$, and two functors $u,v:X\to F$ such that $[u]\ne[v]$ in $\mathrm{Cat}_{\mathrm{hot}}$, while $Bu$ and $Bv$ are unpointedly homotopic. In particular fibrancy of the target does not imply injectivity of
\[
 \pi_0\mathrm{Fun}(X,F)\longrightarrow[BX,BF].
\]

The proposed classification by two-types and two-groupoids — The strict $2$-groupoid $\mathbf B^2C_2$ with one object, one $1$-arrow, and $2$-automorphism group $C_2$ is not local in either transformation convention. For $X=\mathbf BC_2$, the canonical comparison has a singleton domain and a two-element codomain:
\[
 \Hom_{\mathcal H_2}(\mathbf BC_2,\mathbf B^2C_2)
 \longrightarrow [BC_2,K(C_2,2)]. \tag{E.1.1}
\]
Consequently the statement that all strict $2$-groupoids are local is false.

The groupoid reflection in every strict dimension — For $1\leq n\leq\infty$, let $\Pi X$ be the groupoid with generators the $1$-cells of $X$, relations for their strict compositions, and the relation $f=g$ for every $2$-cell $f\Rightarrow g$. The strict functor $\eta_X:X\to\Pi X$ induces the fundamental groupoid of $B_nX$. It gives a reflection
\[
 \Pi:\mathcal H_n\rightleftarrows\Ho(\Grpd):j.
\]
For each groupoid $G$, its canonical comparison is bijective:
\[
 \Hom_{\mathcal H_n}(X,G)\cong[B_nX,BG]. \tag{E.2.1}
\]
The quotient localizes to ordinary homotopy types — The functor $\mathcal H_n\to\Hot_\U$ induced by $B_n$ is localization at Street-nerve weak equivalences, for every $1\leq n\leq\infty$.

Descent of transformations along the R2 quotients — Let $C$ be a strict $n$-category with at most $\mu$ cells in all dimensions, where $\mu$ is infinite. Let $p:G\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma$ be a group quotient such that every homomorphism from $G$ to a group of cardinality at most $\mu$ kills $\ker p$. Restriction along $\mathbf Bp$ is an isomorphism on the categories of strict functors and normal lax transformations from $\mathbf B\Gamma$ and $\mathbf BG$ to $C$. It induces a bijection on transformation-homotopy classes, including the pseudo convention.

Invariant small ind-objects in every strict dimension — For $1\leq n\leq\infty$, the Street-nerve invariant $\U$-small ind-objects of $\mathcal H_n$ are exactly the ind-objects of ordinary groupoids. For an invariant diagram $(K_i)_{i\in I}$ the canonical morphism
\[
 (K_i)_{i\in I}\longrightarrow(\Pi K_i)_{i\in I}
\]
is an isomorphism in $\Ind_\U(\mathcal H_n)$. The same assertion about canonical presheaves holds for arbitrary $\U$-small colimits of representables.

Representable homotopy types and local objects — For each $1\leq n\leq\infty$, a small space $Y$ has $X\mapsto[B_nX,Y]$ representable on $\mathcal H_n$ precisely when $Y$ is a $1$-type. The local objects are exactly those isomorphic in $\mathcal H_n$ to ordinary groupoids, equivalently those whose canonical map $K\to\Pi K$ is an isomorphism there. These conclusions apply to both requested transformation conventions in dimension two.
